messages.content: Complete the following case-report text from the exact point where it stops. Return only the most likely original continuation, without repeating the supplied text, adding headings, quoting the prompt, or explaining your approach. This is a text-continuation task. Generate at least 998 characters of continuation text after repeated whitespace is collapsed. Aim for about 1398 characters (approximately 168 whitespace-separated words). This is a minimum-length request, not a maximum. If the next sentence or paragraph ends before the minimum is reached, continue the case narrative. Do not pad, repeat, add a preface, or discuss the requested length.

A 52-year-old man presented with a 1-year history of persistent watery diarrhoea (3–4 episodes daily), accompanied by acid reflux, upper abdominal discomfort, and numbness in the distal extremities. Previous gastroenterological investigations, including upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, had led to diagnoses of bile reflux gastritis and a colonic lesion treated by endoscopic submucosal dissection. Histopathological examination of the resected lesion showed a sessile serrated lesion with dysplasia. His diarrhoea remained refractory to symptomatic treatment. During the preceding 6 months, he also developed progressive exertional dyspnoea, fatigue, and unintentional weight loss of 10 kg. His medical history included gout and nephrolithiasis. There was no known family history of amyloidosis. On examination, his blood pressure was 80/46 mmHg and heart rate was 52 beats/min, with no other specific cardiopulmonary or abdominal abnormalities. message.content: and ECG revealed low-voltage QRS complexes in the limb leads with a PR interval of 240 ms. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a thickened interventricular septum (14 mm) and left atrial dilation with preserved ejection fraction of 55% and a sparkling myocardial texture. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed diffuse subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement and abnormal myocardial nulling at 0 ms, consistent with amyloid infiltration. Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation revealed a monoclonal IgG-kappa band, and serum free light chain assay showed a markedly elevated kappa free light chain (186 mg/L) with a kappa/lambda ratio of 42.3. Bone marrow biopsy demonstrated 18% clonal plasma cells. Abdominal fat pad aspiration yielded Congo red–positive amorphous deposits with apple-green birefringence under polarised light, and mass spectrometry confirmed AL (lambda) type amyloid. The patient was initiated on daratumumab, cyclophosphamide, and dexamethasone. At 6-month follow-up, his diarrhoea had resolved, blood pressure improved to 112/70 mmHg, NT-proBNP decreased to 142 pg/mL, and echocardiographic wall thickness reduced to 11 mm, indicating a favourable haematological and organ response.
